 About Us
 10x Team connects top independent professionals with leading AI labs to accelerate innovation in artificial intelligence.  Key Responsibilities

 About You

 - Based in the EU or UK

 - Analytical, detail-oriented, and able to provide structured, constructive feedback
 - Available 8–20 hours per week, comfortable with remote and asynchronous collaboration
 Why Join 10x Team?

 Job Description
 The Regional Lean Business Analyst is a deployment-embedded role, not a desk-based reporting function. You will spend significant time on manufacturing floors alongside the RDL and Lean Manufacturing Specialist during site diagnostics and improvement cycles, directly observing processes, engaging with production teams, and gathering the data to turn into action. During active deployments, the Regional Lean Business Analyst works under the direction of the Regional Deployment Leader as part of the integrated triad. What makes this role distinct is the combination of genuine lean deployment experience with the analytical capability to substantiate what the team finds on the floor. You need to understand what you are looking at on the floor before you can structure the data behind it. The right candidate is someone who has led or participated meaningfully in lean or continuous improvement deployments and brings enough technical fluency to build the tools, dashboards, and tracking mechanisms that make improvement outcomes visible and defensible.
 Key Responsibilities
 Lean Deployment Execution
 - Deploy on-site alongside the RDL and Lean Manufacturing Specialist during diagnostic and improvement cycles at Americas manufacturing sites, serving as the analytical backbone of the deployment trio. 
 - Participate and conduct direct floor-level process observation, time studies, material and information flow analysis, and Gemba-based problem identification as an active member of the deployment team. 
 - Translate floor-level observations into structured problem statements and quantified opportunity assessments that the triad uses to prioritize improvement efforts with site leadership. 
 - Support the design and implementation of lean countermeasures including standard work development, visual management systems, pull-based material flow, and quality process improvements in collaboration with site teams. 
 - Contribute to diagnostic synthesis documents, deployment readouts, and site leadership presentations that communicate findings, recommendations, and results clearly and credibly. 
 - Analytical Support and Digital Tooling
 - Gather, clean, and structure production, quality, planning, and logistics data from site systems (SAP, MES, LIMS, and local databases) to support deployment diagnostics and ongoing improvement tracking. 
 - Build analytical models and dashboards using tools such as Python, Power BI, or equivalent platforms that help the deployment team identify process bottlenecks, capacity constraints, yield losses, and planning gaps. 
 - Develop tracking mechanisms and visual reporting that replace manual processes with clear, real-time visibility into deployment progress and site performance. 
 - Manage deployment project tracking through Jira or equivalent tools, maintaining clear visibility into action item status, ownership, timelines, and completion evidence across concurrent site engagements. 
 - Savings Substantiation and Reporting
 - Partner with site controllers and the OEX control tower to substantiate improvement outcomes using the OEX Value Recognition Framework, ensuring savings claims are categorized accurately and supported by verifiable evidence. 
 - Prepare financial impact summaries for deployment readouts and leadership reporting, translating operational improvements into the gross profit recovery and cost reduction language that the organization tracks. 
 - Build and maintain regional tracking tools that provide cumulative visibility into the Americas deployment portfolio, savings trajectory, and site maturity progression. 
 - Capability Building and Knowledge Management
 - Develop reusable analytical templates, diagnostic data request packages, and deployment playbooks that accelerate future site engagements and reduce the ramp-up time for new team members. 
 - Train site-level personnel on basic data collection protocols and self-service reporting tools so that improvement visibility persists after the deployment team transitions out. 
 - Contribute to the evolution of OEX’s analytical methodology, incorporating new tools and emerging best practices as the function matures. 
 Qualifications
 - Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Data Science, Business Analytics, or a related quantitative discipline. 
 - 8+ years of professional experience in manufacturing operations with direct, hands-on involvement in lean or continuous improvement deployments, kaizen events, or structured operational improvement programs at the floor level. 
 - Strong analytical and data fluency with demonstrated ability to build and apply tools such as Python, Power BI, or equivalent platforms for data manipulation, visualization, and operational analysis. Candidates with deep lean deployment backgrounds who can demonstrate rapid self-directed technical skill acquisition will be considered alongside those with established proficiency. 
 - Experience extracting and working with data from ERP systems (SAP strongly preferred) and manufacturing execution systems. 
 - Working knowledge of project management tools such as Jira, Smartsheet, or equivalent, with experience tracking multi-workstream improvement programs. 
 - Comfort operating in a manufacturing floor environment during deployments, including direct interaction with production operators, supervisors, quality engineers, and site planners. 
 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex operational and analytical findings into clear narratives for both technical and executive audiences. 
 - Willingness to travel 30–50% within the Americas region during active deployment periods. Occasional international travel for cross-regional collaboration. 
 Preferred Qualifications
 - Experience in regulated manufacturing environments such as life sciences, diagnostics, or pharmaceuticals. 
 - Direct experience operating within a structured production system methodology such as the Toyota Production System, Danaher Business System, or comparable enterprise-wide operational excellence framework, with an understanding of how deployment-based improvement differs from project-based continuous improvement. 
 - Working familiarity with manufacturing cost structures, standard costing, and the mechanics of how operational improvements translate to financial outcomes at the site level. 
 - Experience with SQL for direct database queries and data extraction. 
 - Exposure to both instrument manufacturing and biological or pharmaceutical manufacturing environments. 
 - Master’s degree in a relevant quantitative field. 
 Additional Details
 This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least June 25, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted.
The full-time equivalent pay range for this position is $124,160.00 - $232,800.00/yr plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.  Entreprise :
 Safran Nacelles est l'un des deux principaux intégrateurs mondiaux de nacelles de moteurs d'avion. Avec plus de 19 000 équipements en service, Safran Nacelles propose une gamme de nacelles
 La nacelle est à l'interface entre le moteur et l'avion. Elle est un système complexe qui assure de multiples fonctions gérées dans un environnement sévère (températures extrêmes, contraintes dimensionnelles) et qui doit rester la plus légère possible. La nacelle canalise les flux d'air du moteur et le protège. Elle contribue au freinage de l'avion durant la phase d'atterrissage (inverseurs de poussée) et à l'atténuation des émissions sonores de l'avion. La nacelle doit également garantir un accès facile au moteur pour sa maintenance.
 Les 3 500 collaborateurs de Safran Nacelles mettent leur passion au service des clients. Grâce à leur expertise et leur savoir-faire, l'entreprise développe les nacelles adaptées à chaque type d'aéronef : avions régionaux, avions d'affaires, avions commerciaux de plus de 100 places, moyens et longs courriers.
 Safran Nacelles MOROCCO est spécialisée dans la production de pièces composites et l'assemblage d’inverseurs/nacelles et de sous-ensembles des nacelles.

 Company Description Duggan Associates is an international training and advisory firm specializing in Operational Excellence through advanced Value Stream Design. The organization focuses on building client capability rather than traditional, dependency-based consulting. Teams are trained to integrate physical flow and information flow to achieve sustainable, end-to-end speed. Duggan Associates has deep expertise in complex environments, with a strong focus on Mixed Model Value Streams and advanced Lean Manufacturing principles. Applicants will join a firm known for practical, high-impact methods that drive measurable performance improvements.

On a day-to-day basis, the consultant assists senior team members with data collection, process mapping, and analysis of value streams in manufacturing and complex environments.  - Experience or demonstrated interest in Consulting and Management Consulting, including working with clients to diagnose problems and implement solutions.
 - Coaching and facilitation skills, with the ability to support training sessions and guide teams through new processes and tools.

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations management, business, industrial engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
 - Prior exposure to Lean Manufacturing, value stream mapping, or continuous improvement projects is preferred but not required.

 Victoria R.
 Victoria R.
 Expert in Sales and Leadership Recruitment Services | Smart Industry
 Continuous Improvement Manager – Food & Beverage Manufacturing
 Location: Remote / Field-Based — UK or Ireland home base, working across EMEA
 Travel: ~90% — onsite at customer plants Monday to Friday, minimum 42 weeks per year
 Sector: Food & Beverage / FMCG Manufacturing | Connected Worker Technology | Industrial SaaS
 Package: Competitive base + quarterly bonuses + car allowance
 This is not a Continuous Improvement Lead vacancy — and it is not a desk job. We're looking for proven manufacturing leaders — CI and Lean Leaders, Production Managers, Plant Managers — to become Operational Excellence Coaches at a global manufacturing software business, spending ~90% of their time on customer factory floors across EMEA, Monday to Friday, at least 42 weeks a year. 
 If that travel commitment excites you rather than puts you off, read on. Have you spent your career driving OEE, Lean and TPM results on the shop floor — and outgrown the four walls of a single site? This role puts you inside a different factory every month, leading intensive frontline transformations for some of the world's best-known food and beverage manufacturers.
 Why this space matters now 
 Manufacturers everywhere are fighting the same battle: labour shortages, high frontline turnover, and productivity targets that can't be met by capital investment alone. Connected worker technology has become one of the fastest-growing categories in industrial software because it attacks that problem directly — engaging frontline teams, making performance visible in real time, and unlocking capacity plants didn't know they had. The companies deploying it need coaches who have genuinely run shop floors, not career consultants.
 The client 
 Our client is the market leader in connected workforce technology for manufacturing — a global SaaS business whose platform is live in well over 1,000 plants worldwide. Their customers include PepsiCo, Kraft Heinz and Coca-Cola alongside hundreds of mid-sized food, beverage and CPG manufacturers. Their deployment model is famous for speed: measurable results — on average a double-digit OEE point gain and productivity improvements approaching 30% — inside the first 90 days. The coaching team is the engine of that model.
 The Role 
 As an Operational Excellence Coach, you'll lead end-to-end frontline transformations across the EMEA customer base. This is emphatically not a desk job: you'll spend around 90% of your time on customer factory floors, coaching everyone from operators to plant directors on how to win with the platform. You'll manage 5–6 customer accounts at a time through their 90-day engagement cycles, including intensive four-week onsite deployments at each site. It's fast, high-accountability work with visible results — and a clear path into senior coaching and leadership roles.
 Key Responsibilities 
 - Lead hands-on onsite deployments, taking multiple customer plants through fast-paced 90-day transformation cycles
 - Coach and influence frontline operators, supervisors and plant leadership to adopt Lean behaviours and get full value from the platform
 - Run shop-floor Kaizen events and continuous improvement rituals grounded in Lean, Six Sigma, TPM and Operational Excellence frameworks
 - Partner with plant leadership to challenge the status quo, take on difficult site cultures, and deliver measurable productivity and OEE gains
 - Build trusted relationships from the production line through to senior leadership
 About You 
 Essential: 
 - Substantial hands-on manufacturing leadership experience — as a Plant Manager, Production Manager, CI/Lean Leader, OpEx or TPM deployment leader, or Manufacturing Consultant. You must have run a shop floor, not just contributed to one
 - A track record in Lean, Six Sigma, TPM or Operational Excellence, with measurable productivity and OEE improvements you can point to
 - Evidence of being a genuine top performer — someone with a history of overachievement and progression, not a steady contributor
 - The presence and confidence to challenge senior executives and inspire frontline operators alike
 - Willingness to sustain ~90% travel: field-based Monday to Friday, a minimum of 42 weeks per year, across EMEA
 - Full professional fluency in English
 Preferred: 
 - Deep roots in Food & Beverage or CPG manufacturing (Automotive experience also valued)
 - Experience deploying improvement programmes across multiple sites or environments
 - Military leadership background combined with manufacturing or engineering experience
 Why Apply

 Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.
 A Day in the Life
 At Medtronic you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation, while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world.
The Medtronic Clinical and Regulatory Solutions (MCRS) business is looking for a motivated Senior Program Manager with strong Lean Six Sigma expertise (Black Belt preferred) to be part of a high-performing team driving organizational transformation and excellence in the regulatory and clinical functions. In this role, you will leverage your project management expertise, Lean Six Sigma methodologies, and leadership skills to establish and optimize processes across teams, evolve organizational structure, and drive maturity in support of more efficient and compliant operations. You'll lead initiatives like establishing shared service centers and centers of excellence that transform how our organization operates. The work you do will impact patients globally and help support Medtronic's mission of alleviating pain, restoring health, and extending life for millions.
This role requires a results-driven leader with deep process improvement expertise and strong interpersonal and analytical skills. The ideal candidate has a Lean mindset, thrives in ambiguous environments, and is passionate about driving measurable operational efficiencies through data, process mapping, and structured problem-solving. A strong background in business transformation, value stream design, and stakeholder engagement is essential. The ideal candidate will have an unrelenting desire to improve our business and an ability to take leadership in ambiguous environments with minimal SME support. The candidate will be motivated and must have exceptional soft skills that will be used to work with various cross-functional teams while engaging senior-leader (Dir, Sr Dir, VP) stakeholders.
We value what makes you unique. Be a part of a company that thinks differently to solve problems, make progress, and deliver meaningful innovations.
 Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:
 - Lead end-to-end process transformation initiatives across Clinical, Regulatory, and Quality functions, focusing on shared service optimization, standardization, and scalability.
 - Facilitate cross-functional value stream mapping and process redesign workshops to identify inefficiencies, eliminate waste, and create integrated, future-state processes.
 - Apply Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methodologies to diagnose root causes, implement sustainable improvements, and quantify business value.
 - Manage large projects or processes with considerable latitude in determining deliverables, with limited oversight from manager.
 - Coach, review and delegate work to lower-level specialists, acting as a team leader for organizational change initiatives.
 - Work cross-functionally with Clinical, Regulatory, Quality, and others, to drive more effective interactions between various parts of the business and build integrated processes.
 - Structure organizational needs by documenting clear milestones and driving actions to meet those milestones.
 - Quickly discern competing needs of stakeholders and negotiate solutions that bring about the best value to Medtronic overall.
 - Identify how data may be used to identify and/or track opportunities, detect broad trends, and communicate meaningful stories to stakeholders.
 - Navigate ambiguity and complex, technical processes with limited support from subject-matter experts.
 - Maintain engagement with senior leaders across the organization through regular communications that bring clarity and momentum on actions needed.
 - Identify potential programs or opportunities, quantify the possible return on investment, and present proposals to senior leaders.
 - Support business model innovation as a strategic-thinking advisor and contribute to defining the direction for strategic initiatives, new businesses, and operational plans.
 Required Knowledge and Experience:
 - Bachelor's degree plus 7+ years of relevant program management experience (advanced degree with 5+ years relevant experience) or 2+ years of experience operating at a senior manager level
 - Lean Six Sigma certification (Black Belt preferred) - experience applying Lean in regulated or complex domains (e.g., medical device, pharma, healthcare)
 - Preferred background in operations, or other process-intensive environments
 - Strong experience with value stream mapping, root cause analysis, and structured problem solving
 - Demonstrated success in organizational transformation initiatives, particularly establishing shared service centers or centers of excellence
 - Proven track record negotiating and implementing strategic solutions to meet anticipated business needs with predictability 
 - Using project management tools to manage scope, cost, resources, and schedules
 - Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to ask critical questions without being the subject matter expert
 - Ability to lead, influence, and elevate the performance of team members outside direct line of reporting
 Additional valuable experience includes familiarity with regulatory or clinical processes and requirements, as well as a working knowledge of financial principles, quality systems, and medical device regulations.

 Organization Overview Company Description
 At QAD | Redzone , we don't just provide software; we transform shop floors. We are the leading Connected Workforce solution in manufacturing, enabling factories to achieve hard dollar savings in productivity, compliance, and reliability within 90 days. We believe that technology is only as good as the people using it. That’s why we partner with manufacturing plants to change behaviors, elevate frontline workers, and drive sustainable operational excellence.
 Job Description
 We are seeking a high-energy, ambitious Operational Excellence (OpEx) Coach / Manager to drive end-to-end frontline transformations across our EMEA customer base. This is not a desk job or a standard 40-hour work week. You will spend 90% of your time on the factory floor, coaching everyone from frontline operators to plant leadership on how to win using the Redzone platform. You will simultaneously manage 5 to 6 customer accounts across their 90-day engagement cycles, spending intense, targeted 4-week physical onsite deployments with each.
 Note: Out of the three open vacancies, one specific position prefers full professional fluency in Mandarin alongside English to support our expanding APAC manufacturing footprint.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Drive Behavior Change: Coach, mentor, and influence frontline operators, supervisors, and plant managers to adopt Lean behaviors and maximize the Redzone platform.
 - Execute Onsite Deployments: Lead intensive, hands-on onsite implementations, managing multiple customer accounts through high-stakes, fast-paced transformation cycles.
 - Deliver Measurable ROI: Partner with plant leadership to challenge the status quo, tackle difficult site cultures, and unlock immediate productivity and efficiency gains.
 - Facilitate Kaizen & Lean Rituals: Run shop-floor continuous improvement events, coaching teams on Lean, Six Sigma, TPM, and Operational Excellence frameworks.
 Qualifications
 Qualifications & Requirements
 - Proven Factory Leadership: Substantial hands-on experience as a Plant Manager, Production Manager, Continuous Improvement/Lean Leader, or Manufacturing Consultant. You must have run a shop floor, not just contributed to it.
 - Industry Domain Expertise: Deep roots in manufacturing sectors; experience in Food & Beverage or CPG is highly preferred, though Automotive experience is valued.
 - Demonstrated Agility & Growth: A proven track record of career progression and adaptive flexibility, ideally shown through successful transitions across different manufacturing environments every 2–3 years.
 - Uncompromising Travel Flexibility: Willingness and hunger to sustain ~90% travel (away from home Monday morning through Friday night, minimum 42 weeks a year).
 - Language Skills: Full professional fluency in English is required for all roles. Fluency in Mandarin is desired for the specialized APAC support vacancy.
 - Expert Communicator: Exceptional presence with the confidence to challenge senior executives and inspire frontline operators alike.
 Additional Information
 Location: Remote (EMEA Field-Based)
 Travel: ~90% (Minimum 42 weeks/year, Monday–Friday field travel)
 Compensation: £70,000 – £85,000 base salary + quarterly bonuses + car allowance
 About QAD And QAD Redzone
 QAD Inc. is a leading provider of adaptive, cloud-based enterprise software and services for global manufacturing companies. Global manufacturers face ever-increasing disruption caused by technology-driven innovation and changing consumer preferences. In order to survive and thrive, manufacturers must be able to innovate and change business models at unprecedented rates of speed. QAD calls these companies Adaptive Manufacturing Enterprises.
QAD Redzone helps to enable QAD’s vision for the Adaptive Enterprise. Labor productivity improvements directly impact efficiency. Productive and empowered employees increase the effective capacity of your plant and accelerate time to productivity for new employees giving manufacturers the agility to increase production beyond what was previously possible without having to invest in production equipment or new plants, and reduce the amount and impact of employee attrition. Empowered employees with a growth mindset take extreme ownership of challenges that impact their production goals, creating resilience in the face of disruption.

 Overview
 The Director – Business Process Improvement for Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) is responsible for process evaluation and standardization, establishing performance metrics, identifying productivity enhancements, developing and maintaining process documentation, and driving overall continuous improvement. This role partners closely with operational leaders, IT, analytics, compliance, and executive stakeholders to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce manual work, enhance accuracy, strengthen controls, and improve financial outcomes.
The Director – Business Process Improvement serves as both a strategic leader and operational architect—driving enterprise process improvement initiatives while ensuring efforts align with organizational goals, regulatory requirements, and the realities of healthcare operations. This role oversees operational workflows that align with strategic growth goals, project prioritization, vendor collaboration and procurement, planning, change management, and long-term optimization efforts across end-to-end revenue cycle functions.
Job Highlights
 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES : (The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation)
 Strategic Leadership
 Translates executive vision into an actionable, measurable roadmap for operational excellence across multiple departments.
Identifies high-impact automation and process improvement opportunities across the revenue cycle, including patient access, coding, billing, claims management, payment posting, denials, collections, and reporting.
Builds multi-year roadmaps focused on scalability, operational efficiency, and measurable ROI.
Establishes governance frameworks for intake, prioritization, implementation, and monitoring.
Serves as a strategic advisor to executive leadership regarding process transformation opportunities and operational modernization.
 Process Optimization and Operational Excellence
 Leads end-to-end process analysis to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, rework, and operational risk areas.
Standardizes workflows and operational practices to support scalable automation solutions.
Drives Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies across RCM operations.
Partners with operational leaders to redesign workflows that improve productivity, quality, turnaround time, and employee experience.
Develops and monitors KPIs related to automation performance, operational efficiency, financial outcomes, and adoption.
 Design and Implementation
 Defines complex problem statements, develops success metrics, and presents outcomes to senior leadership.
Maps out end to end current and future state workflows to identify bottlenecks, waste, and friction points.
Develops and maintains process documentation, including process maps, standard operating procedures, and performance metrics.
Collaborates with IT, data, analytics, and vendors to ensure successful solution design, testing, implementation, and support.
Optimizes reporting, dashboards, and updates to show status, risks, and impact.
 Stakeholder Partnership and Change Management
 Builds strong partnerships across operations, finance, compliance, IT, analytics, and executive leadership.
Translates operational challenges into scalable solutions and actionable business requirements.
Leads organizational change management efforts related to process transformation and adoption.
Communicates project progress, risks, outcomes, and ROI to senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Drives a culture of innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement leveraging data to inform decisions and prioritize initiatives.
Coordinates, educates, and integrates data management to support leaders.
 Qualifications
 KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES (KSAs): 
 Required
 - Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare administration, information systems, finance, operations, or a related field. 
 - 7+ years of experience in healthcare revenue cycle operations, process improvement, automation, or operational transformation. 
 - 7+ years of leadership experience managing projects, programs, teams, or enterprise initiatives. 
 - Strong knowledge of healthcare revenue cycle functions, workflows, payer processes, and regulatory considerations. 
 - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders. 
 - Strong analytical, operational, and strategic problem-solving skills. 
 - Excellent communication, presentation, and executive-facing skills. 
 Preferred
 - Master’s degree (MBA, MHA, or related field). 
 - Experience with Epic, Cerner, Athenahealth, Meditech, or other healthcare systems. 
 - Lean Six Sigma, PMP, or related certifications. 
 - Experience leading AI-enabled workflow transformation initiatives. 
 - Familiarity with healthcare compliance requirements including HIPAA and CMS regulations. 
 - Experience implementing automation technologies and process improvement initiatives within complex healthcare environments.

 - Frequent Sitting 
 - Frequent hand, finger movement 
 - Use office equipment (in office or remote) 
 - Communicate verbally and in writing

 Suivre 
 Entreprise :
 Aya Gold & Silver est un producteur d’argent canadien en pleine croissance qui exerce ses activités au Royaume du Maroc.
 Aya est la seule société minière purement argentifère cotée à la Bourse de Toronto. Elle exploite la mine d’argent Zgounder à forte teneur et explore ses terrains situés le long de l’Accident Sud-Atlasique à fort potentiel, dont plusieurs renferment d’anciennes mines productrices et des ressources historiques. En plus de ses actifs miniers marocains, Aya détient aussi le projet aurifère Tijirit situé en Mauritanie, qui avance à l’étape de l’étude de faisabilité.
 Dans le cadre de son expansion, AYA Gold & Silver est en phase de renforcer ses équipes par des compétences dans plusieurs métiers, notamment la maintenance.
 Poste :
 Mission principale: 
 Assurer la planification, le suivi et l'optimisation des opérations de maintenance des matériels roulants afin de garantir leur disponibilité, leur fiabilité et leur sécurité, tout en contribuant à la maîtrise des coûts et à l'amélioration continue des performances du service maintenance
 Taches principales: 
 • Assurer le suivi de l'état des matériels roulants et veiller à l'application des exigences de sécurité et d'environnement dans les activités de maintenance.
 • Coordonner et suivre les opérations de maintenance, urgences, préventive, corrective et prédictive des matériels roulants.
 • Participer à l’analyse des indicateurs de performance (disponibilité, fiabilité, coûts, temps d’arrêt, etc.) et proposer des actions d’amélioration adaptées.
 • Suivre et mettre à jour les plans et programmes de maintenance.
 • Participer à la gestion des risques techniques liés aux matériels roulants et proposer des mesures préventives appropriées.
 • Assurer le suivi technique des interventions réalisées par les équipes internes et les prestataires externes.
 • Participer à la préparation des cahiers des charges et à l'évaluation technique des offres d'achat de pièces de rechange (PDR), équipements et prestations de maintenance.
 • Assurer le suivi des besoins, des consommations et des commandes de pièces de rechange afin de garantir la disponibilité des stocks stratégiques.
 • Réaliser les analyses de défaillance et contribuer à la mise en œuvre des actions correctives et préventives.
 • Participer à la mise en place et à l'amélioration des procédures, méthodes et outils de maintenance.
 • Contribuer à la formation technique et au développement des compétences des équipes de maintenance.
 • Assurer le reporting des activités de maintenance et élaborer les tableaux de bord techniques destinés à la hiérarchie.
 • Participer aux projets de renouvellement, de réhabilitation ou d'amélioration des matériels roulants.
 • Assurer le suivi des audits QSE et des plans d’actions associés
 Rôles & Responsabilités HSE 
 • Porter les Équipements de Protection Individuelle (EPI) requis sur le poste de travail.
 • Appliquer les standards de sécurité ZMSM / AYA Gold & Silver.
 • Respecter la réglementation en vigueur (les contrôles réglementaires).
 • Analyser les risques au niveau du service sur les volets santé, conditions de travail, sécurité et environnement.
 • Mettre en œuvre le plan d’action annuel QSE sur son périmètre.
 • Assurer une présence sur chantier lors d’opérations de maintenance à haut risque ou dans les ateliers pour les visites de contrôle.
 Profil recherché :
 Savoir : 
 • Maîtrise des techniques de maintenance des engins souterrains : mécanique, hydraulique, pneumatique, électricité, électronique et systèmes de transmission.
 • Bonne connaissance des stratégies de maintenance : préventive, corrective, prédictive, conditionnelle et overhaul.
 • Connaissance des recommandations et procédures des constructeurs pour les différents types d'engins.
 • Maîtrise des méthodes d'amélioration continue appliquées à la maintenance (TPM, Lean Maintenance, RCA, AMDEC).
 • Connaissance des principes de planification et d'organisation des activités de maintenance.
 • Notions de gestion budgétaire et de suivi des coûts de maintenance (OPEX et CAPEX).
 • Maîtrise des outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO), des tableaux de bord et des indicateurs de performance.
 • Connaissance des normes HSE applicables aux activités minières souterraines.
 • Connaissance des techniques d'analyse des défaillances et de fiabilisation des équipements.
 • Maîtrise des outils informatiques et bureautiques (Excel avancé, logiciels de reporting et d'analyse).
 Savoir-faire : 
 • Élaborer et suivre les plans de maintenance préventive, corrective et conditionnelle des matériels roulants.
 • Planifier et coordonner les interventions de maintenance en collaboration avec les équipes opérationnelles.
 • Analyser les indicateurs de performance maintenance (disponibilité, fiabilité, MTBF, MTTR, coûts de maintenance).
 • Réaliser des analyses de pannes et identifier les causes racines des défaillances récurrentes.
 • Proposer et mettre en œuvre des actions d'amélioration visant à accroître la disponibilité et la fiabilité des équipements.
 • Participer à la préparation et au suivi des budgets de maintenance.
 • Établir les spécifications techniques et participer à l'évaluation des offres relatives aux pièces de rechange, équipements et prestations de maintenance.
 • Assurer le suivi des stocks stratégiques et des commandes de pièces de rechange.
 • Participer aux projets d'amélioration, de modernisation et de réhabilitation des matériels roulants.
 • Élaborer et analyser les rapports techniques et les tableaux de bord de maintenance.
 • Assurer la coordination avec les services Production, Magasin, Achats, HSE et les prestataires externes.
 • Veiller à l'application des procédures de maintenance et des exigences de sécurité.
 Savoir être : 
 • Rigueur et sens de l'organisation.
 • Esprit d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes.
 • Réactivité et capacité à gérer les priorités opérationnelles.
 • Autonomie dans la conduite des missions techniques.
 • Esprit d'équipe et capacité à travailler dans un environnement multidisciplinaire.
 • Bonnes capacités de communication et de rédaction technique.
 • Sens des responsabilités et engagement envers la sécurité.
 • Force de proposition et orientation amélioration continue.
 • Capacité d'adaptation aux contraintes du milieu minier souterrain.
 • Gestion efficace du stress et des situations d'urgence.
 • Respect des règles, procédures et standards de qualité.
 • Culture HSE forte et exemplarité dans l'application des règles de sécurité.

 Job Description Summary
 The Quality Leader is responsible for the successful deployment of the Built-In Quality (BiQ) Playbook across value stream warehouses. Built-In Quality is a systematic approach designed to improve quality and optimize efficiency by minimizing waste and maximizing value for the customer.
This role serves as a technical partner to warehouse operations, ensuring that all material handling and storage processes are robust, compliant, and error-proofed. The Quality Leader will lead nonconformance response and resolution activities, including NCR investigations, structured problem solving, Corrective Action and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes, and the use of CIMs, RCAs, and PSRs to eliminate recurrence and improve process capability. You will be the primary driver of quality rigor at the point of activity, fostering a culture of "Zero Defects" and continuous improvement. Success in this role relies on collaborating effectively across supply chain, operations, repair, engineering, and shop teams to drive disciplined, high-quality execution.
 Job Description
 Roles and Responsibilities
 - BiQ Playbook Deployment: Drive the end-to-end implementation of the BiQ Playbook within warehouse operations. Translate strategic quality requirements into clear, executable standard work for logistics and inventory teams to ensure process consistency. Lead the deployment of the 15 core elements of the BiQ Playbook across all assigned warehouses. Ensure each element is fully integrated into daily operations and monitor their effectiveness to guarantee that the framework is not only implemented but consistently operational and delivering intended results.
 - Audit Management: Conduct regular quality audits to verify compliance with internal standards and the BiQ framework. Identify process gaps, document findings, and drive the necessary corrective actions to maintain high levels of operational maturity and audit readiness.
 - Quality Gate Management: Establish and oversee critical Quality Gates within the material flow. Ensure that every transaction—from receiving and picking to packing and shipping—is verified against standard criteria to prevent quality escapes.
 - NCR Investigations & RCA: Manage the triage and investigation of Non-Conformances (NCRs) within the assigned value streams. Lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) activities to identify systemic failures and implement sustainable solutions, moving beyond containment to permanent process improvements.
 - Zero Defect Initiatives: Partner with cross-functional warehouse teams to reduce scrap and rework. Utilize operational metrics to identify trend-based risks and prioritize improvement projects that enhance "First-Time Quality."
 - Operational Training & Culture: Act as a technical quality coach on the shop floor. Train warehouse personnel on BiQ methodologies and ensure that quality ownership is embedded at every level of the material handling process.
 - Lead rigorous root cause investigations for warehouse quality escapes such as damage, wrong part, incomplete material, or shipping discrepancies, driving sustainable Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) to prevent recurrence.
 - Analyze quality trends and performance metrics to identify systemic risks, reporting findings to leadership to drive data-based improvement initiatives.
 - Facilitate quality guidance and training for warehouse personnel promoting an SQDC culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement across the operation.
 Required Qualifications
 - Bachelor’s degree in Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, or related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
 - Proven experience in a quality or operations-focused role within a manufacturing or logistics setting.
 - Strong practical knowledge of quality management systems (QMS) and structured problem-solving tools (e.g., 8D, RCA, 5-Why).
 - Experience with ERP systems and warehouse management platforms.
 - Ability to translate complex quality requirements into simple, actionable process instructions.
 - Strong communication, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 - Strong knowledge of quality systems, Lean principles, corrective action processes, and nonconformance management.
 Desired Characteristics
 - Direct experience implementing Built-In Quality (BiQ) or Lean manufacturing frameworks.
 - Strong capability to influence change without direct authority in a fast-paced warehouse environment.
 - Data-driven mindset with the ability to analyze operational performance and turn findings into improvement actions.
 - Excellent communication skills with the ability to lead training sessions and facilitate collaborative meetings.
 - Demonstrated commitment to a "Zero Defect" mindset and proactive risk identification.
 - Experience leading audits and managing CAPA systems.
 - Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience
 Key Competencies
 - Quality leadership
 - Analytical thinking
 - Root cause problem-solving
 - Attention to detail
 - Cross-functional influence
 - Customer focus
 - Process improvement
 - Risk management
 - Change management

• Faciliter les revues de jalons : Préparer et animer les points qualité en amont des comités de pilotage, avec des synthèses claires sur les risques qualité et les actions correctives ;

 - Très bonne maîtrise des outils bureautiques dont Excel/PPT
 - Connaissance et expérience dans les environnements industriels auto/aéro/ferroviaire

 About The Role
 10x.team connects expert freelancers with leading AI labs building next-generation models. We are looking for knowledgeable operational excellence professionals based in the EU or UK to enhance the accuracy, depth, and real-world relevance of AI-powered business systems.

 Job Description
 BioVectra, now part of Agilent’s Advanced Therapeutics Division (ATD), is a CDMO producing active pharmaceutical ingredients at clinical-to-commercial scale across microbial fermentation, small molecules, plasmid DNA, mRNA, LNP, and sterile fill, operating from Charlottetown, PEI and Windsor, Nova Scotia. This posting is for the BioVectra assignment within Agilent's Operational Excellence (OEx) function.
Agilent’s Operational Excellence function builds and embeds the production system on the manufacturing floor. The function exists to convert operational performance into capacity the divisions can sell. The Operational Excellence Lead owns this build across the full value stream, from fermentation through downstream recovery and purification to release-readiness and leads through depth of expertise with no direct reports. Success depends on influence through the ATD OEX governance model: site leadership owns operating results, while this role owns method, cadence, capability build, and countermeasure discipline. This role works alongside site leadership, not above it.
What You Will Do:
 - Own the production system build across the full value stream at your assigned site or campaigns, from incoming materials through to release-readiness. Begin each deployment with a structured rapid diagnostic that reads the current state of the production system, daily management, and culture through direct observation, operator interviews, and quantitative evidence, and translate the findings into a sequenced deployment roadmap agreed with site operations and quality leadership. 
 - Build and sustain tiered daily management from Tier 1 through Tier 4, leader standard work, visual performance management, Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) boards, and clear KPI ownership at the line, with structured escalation that surfaces and counters abnormality the shift it occurs in. 
 - Own and run the kaizen funnel for your value stream: prioritize, charter, and lead kaizen events and workshops that close KPI gaps in titer and yield stability, fermentation reproducibility, downstream recovery and purification yield, right-first-time execution, changeover through SMED, and the manufacturing-to-quality handoff. 
 - Translate site and business objectives into floor-level priorities through strategy deployment with defined ownership, milestones, countermeasures, and benefits realization. 
 - Connect operational performance to the outcomes the divisions care about: throughput and sellable capacity, on-time-in-full against client commitments, release cycle time, right-first-time, and the inventory, working capital, and cost that follow. Build and maintain a transformation scorecard as the single source of truth for KPI performance, value capture, and countermeasure tracking. 
 - Use MES, electronic batch records, shop-floor data systems, and analytics where they exist to feed the daily management system and surface process abnormality in real time. Identify where digital and AI tools earn a place in daily work, treating them as enablers of the production system rather than a parallel initiative. 
 - Lead and mentor structured problem-solving (A3 and PSP) at the Gemba on the real constraints across the value stream, driving teams through root-cause analysis rather than solving problems for them. 
 - Lead value stream mapping across the batch lifecycle, including the transactional and quality flows where sellable capacity is most often lost, batch-record review, deviation handling, and client response, then install the daily management and standard work that level the work and shorten time to release. 
 - Partner with Quality to support the operating-system elements of the release maturity roadmap, from conventional finished-product testing toward parametric release and real-time release testing where the process knowledge, client alignment, and regulatory pathway support it; the analytical science, filings, and release strategy belong to Quality, while the process understanding, standard work, and flow architecture belong to OEX. 
 - Coach and develop supervisors, operators, and emerging practitioners in standard work, daily management, structured problem-solving, and Lean fundamentals, and build the next generation of certified practitioners at all levels. 
 - Be the method owner for the production-system at your site. Embed standardized ways of working, governance routines, and accountability mechanisms that deliver durable results beyond individual kaizen events. Where leadership owns results and this role owns the method, cadence and countermeasure discipline that produce them. 
 - Anchor to the Biovectra deployment through build and stabilization, embedding deep enough that daily management and standard work hold. As that system matures, contribute to benchmarking and best practice sharing across the North American ATD footprint so hard-won lessons travel. 
 Qualifications
 - Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a life science, chemical or biochemical engineering, or related field
 - 8+ years in a GMP or comparably regulated/complex production environment with direct, hands-on accountability for process performance across the Make value stream, 10+ years will be helpful. 
 - Real depth in microbial fermentation and downstream recovery and purification is the core requirement for this assignment. 
 - Demonstrated, hands-on experience deploying and sustaining a production or business operating system in a line role, whether the Toyota Production System, Lean, or the Danaher Business System (DBS), including strategy deployment, tiered daily management, kaizen, standard work, visual management, and structured problem-solving. 
 - A track record of delivering measurable, sustained business results through transformation, across safety, quality, delivery, throughput, yield, cycle time, cost, or client performance. 
 - Deep command of structured problem-solving and root-cause methodology applied to real process problems, with the credibility to coach operators and influence senior leaders alike. 
 Location, Travel, and On-site Requirements
 - This role is US-based, with significant travel to BioVectra’s sites in Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia, and across the broader ATD footprint as deployment phases require. 
 - This is a Gemba-based role. Expect substantial on-site presence, in the range of fifty to sixty percent depending on deployment phase, including extended periods embedded at a site. 
 It Would Be a Plus If You Also Possess Experience In
 - A CDMO or contract manufacturing environment. 
 - Certification in Lean, Six Sigma, or TPS, or status as a Danaher Business System Certified Practitioner or Advanced Certified Practitioner (CP / ACP). 
 - Certification is welcome but does not substitute for a demonstrated record of building a durable system. 
 Additional Details
 This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least July 28, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted.

 Researcher — Lean 4 & Formal Proof Systems (AI Training)
 About The Role
 What if your deep mathematical expertise could directly shape how AI reasons about formal proofs — pushing the boundary of what machines can understand and verify? We're looking for mathematicians and formal verification specialists to translate sophisticated human-written proofs into Lean 4, working at the cutting edge of mechanized mathematics and AI research.
This is a fully remote, flexible contract role for researchers who love rigor, thrive on precision, and find genuine satisfaction in expressing elegant mathematical arguments in a form a machine can verify.
 - Organization: Alignerr
 - Type: Hourly Contract
 - Location: Remote
 - Commitment: 10–40 hours/week
 What You'll Do
 - Translate informal mathematical proofs into Lean 4 (and related proof systems) with an emphasis on clarity, structure, and correctness
 - Analyze proofs across domains — identifying gaps, hidden assumptions, and formalizable sub-structures
 - Construct formalizations that test the limits of existing proof assistants, especially where automation struggles or fails
 - Investigate and articulate where automated provers break down — due to complexity, missing lemmas, insufficient libraries, or other factors
 - Develop highly readable, reproducible proof scripts aligned with mathematical best practices and proof assistant idioms
 - Collaborate with researchers to design, refine, and evaluate strategies for improving formal verification pipelines
 - Provide guidance on proof decomposition, lemma selection, and structuring techniques for formal models
 - Formalize classical proofs and compare machine-verifiable structures against textbook arguments
 - Surface deeper patterns or generalizations implicit in the original mathematics
 Who You Are
 - Master's degree or higher in Mathematics, Logic, Theoretical Computer Science, or a closely related field
 - Strong foundation in rigorous proof writing and mathematical reasoning — across algebra, analysis, topology, logic, or discrete mathematics
 - Hands-on experience with Lean (Lean 3 or Lean 4), Coq, Isabelle/HOL, Agda, or comparable systems — Lean strongly preferred
 - Deep enthusiasm for formal verification, proof assistants, and the future of mechanized mathematics

This year, Allegion also received Gallup’s With Distinction honor — a designation reserved for a select group of organizations that go above and beyond in building exceptional workplace cultures.
 Process Improvement & Standards Manager-US Remote
 Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. The company does not intend to provide sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B, TN, etc.) for this employment position.
 At Allegion, we recognize that great talent and breakthrough ideas can come from anywhere. That’s why this position offers a flexible remote work arrangement, with occasional on-site visits as needed based on the role. Whether you’re working remotely or collaborating in person, we’re committed to providing the tools, support, and dynamic environment you need to succeed. At Allegion, your career thrives where innovation meets flexibility, empowering you to achieve your goals while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.
 While this is the current structure and we currently have no plans to change, we reserve the right to make changes to the remote schedule as needed at the Company’s discretion.
 Job Summary
 The Process Improvement & Standards Manager will lead a cross-functional team of data analysts and Lean/change specialists to accelerate business performance through aligned metrics, disciplined problem solving, and sustainable process improvement. This role is responsible for building a robust, cascading scorecard that flows from Business Operations Leadership to individual contributors; creating and sustaining a prioritized pipeline of analytics and improvement projects; rolling out Leader Standard Work across Business Operations; facilitating Rapid Improvement Events (RIEs), Kaizen events and problem-solving training; and coaching the team and business leaders through improvement projects to ensure results are delivered and sustained.
 What You Will Do
 Strategy, scorecards & alignment
 - Define, design and implement a single, robust performance scorecard framework that cascades Business Operations Leadership goals through senior leaders to front-line teams and individual contributors.
 - Translate strategic objectives into measurable KPIs, targets and behaviors; ensure owners and cadences are defined for all metrics.
 - Build dashboards and visual management (digital and/or physical) to make performance transparent at all levels.
 - Establish data governance and metric definitions to ensure one version of truth.
 Analytics, project pipeline & delivery
 - Create and manage a prioritized pipeline of analytics and improvement projects aligned to strategic priorities (cost, quality, delivery, safety, customer experience).
 - Define intake, prioritization, business case, resourcing and handoff processes for analytics and improvement work.
 - Oversee delivery of analytics (insights, root-cause analysis, predictive models) and translate findings into actionable improvement plans.
 - Track project ROI and benefits realization; maintain project health and escalation protocols.
 Leader Standard Work, MDI & daily management
 - Lead the rollout and adoption of Leader Standard Work (LSW) across Business Operations including development of role-specific LSW, coaching models and audit/cadence mechanisms (Implementation of MDI throughout Business Operations).
 - Drive daily management practices (Gemba cadence, visual boards, huddles) to sustain improvements and accelerate decision making.
 - Design and monitor LSW/MDI compliance and improvement audits; use findings to close gaps and coach leaders.
 Continuous improvement, events & training
 - Plan, facilitate and/or sponsor RIEs, Kaizen events and structured problem-solving (A3, DMAIC, 8D or equivalent).
 - Develop and deliver problem-solving and Lean curricula for multiple audiences (managers, supervisors, frontline).
 - Support pre/post standard work, control plans and sustainment activities following events.
 Team leadership & coaching
 - Lead, mentor and grow a blended team of data analysts and continuous improvement practitioners.
 - Coach team members and business leaders through complex root-cause analysis, hypothesis testing and countermeasure selection.
 - Recruit, develop and retain high-performing talent; set clear objectives, KPIs and development plans.
 Stakeholder engagement & change management
 - Partner with Business Operations Leadership and cross-functional teams to align priorities, secure resources and remove barriers.
 - Apply change management practices to ensure adoption of new processes, roles and metrics.
 - Communicate progress, wins and lessons learned through executive summaries, reviews and visual performance tools.
 Operational Responsibilities
 - Support functional value stream analyses, staffing models, process improvements and work optimization as needed.
 - Ensure all activities meet corporate EH&S and compliance requirements.
 What You Need To Succeed
 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Data Science, Business Analytics, or related field.
 - 7+ years of combined experience in operational excellence/continuous improvement and data analytics; experience leading both analytics and Lean initiatives.
 - 3+ years’ experience managing or leading teams.
 - Demonstrated success creating and operating cascading scorecards, dashboards and governance for KPIs.
 - Strong analytical skills and experience with analytics tools and languages (SQL, Excel, Power BI/Tableau; Python/R preferred).
 - Lean Six Sigma certification (Green/Black Belt) or equivalent and practical experience facilitating Kaizen/RIEs and structured problem solving.
 - Excellent facilitation, presentation and stakeholder management skills; ability to influence at all levels.
 - Hands-on experience with ERP/WMS/TMS or other operational systems is a plus.
 Nice-to-have
 - Advanced degree in Engineering, Business Analytics, Operations or related field.
 - Experience in distribution, warehousing, logistics or manufacturing operations.
 - Experience with predictive analytics, process mining or advanced statistical methods.
 Working conditions & legal
 - Ability to travel up to 10%-Travel to sites and business units will be required.
 Why work with us
 - Opportunity to lead a visible, strategic function that directly impacts company performance and culture.
 - Strong professional development support and career growth opportunities.
 Allegion is a Great Place to Grow your Career if:  
 - You're seeking a rewarding opportunity that allows you to truly help others.  With thousands of employees and customers around the world, there’s plenty of room to make an impact. As our values state, “this is your business, run with it”. 
 - You’re looking for a company that will invest in your professional development.  As we grow, we want you to grow with us.  
 - You want a culture that promotes work-life balance.  Our employees enjoy generous paid time off, because at Allegion we recognize that you have a full life outside of work!  
 - You want to work for an award-winning company that invests in its people. Allegion is proud to be a recipient of the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award for the second year in a row, recognizing our commitment to employee engagement, strengths-based development, and unlocking human potential. 
 What You’ll Get From Us
 - Health, dental and vision insurance coverage, helping you “be safe, be healthy”   
 - Unlimited Paid Time Off 
 - A commitment to your future with a 401K plan, which currently offers a 6% company match and no vesting period  
 - Health Savings Accounts – Tax-advantaged savings account used for healthcare expenses 
 - Flexible Spending Accounts – Tax-advantaged spending accounts for healthcare and/or dependent daycare expenses 
 - Disability Insurance –Short-Term and Long-Term coverage, paid for by Allegion, provides income replacement for illness or injury 
 - Life Insurance – Term life coverage with the option to purchase supplemental coverage 
 - Tuition Reimbursement   
 - Voluntary Wellness Program – Simply complete wellness activities and earn monetary rewards 
 - Employee Discounts through Perks at Work  
 - Community involvement and opportunities to give back so you can “serve others, not yourself”  
 - Opportunities to leverage your unique strengths through CliftonStrengths assessment & coaching
 Compensation: This range is provided by Allegion. Your actual pay will be based on your skills and experience.
 - The expected Base Salary Range: $81,400-$135,000. The actual compensation will be determined based on experience and other factors permitted by law.

Notre portefeuille de produits s'étend des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways jusqu’aux systèmes intégrés, services sur mesure, infrastructures, signalisation et solutions de mobilité numérique. Nous rejoindre, c'est rejoindre une entreprise bienveillante, responsable et innovante où plus de 80 000 personnes ouvrent la voie à une mobilité plus verte et plus intelligente, dans le monde entier.
Pourriez-vous être le ou la Lean Development Expert à temps plein à La Rochelle que nous recherchons ?
 Votre futur rôle
 Relevez un nouveau défi et mettez à profit votre expertise en Lean Development dans un domaine de pointe. Vous travaillerez avec des équipes dynamiques, collaboratives et engagées, et vous jouerez un rôle clé dans l’amélioration des performances opérationnelles de notre division P&D VLL. Votre impact sera déterminant dans le déploiement des principes et outils Lean, contribuant à transformer nos processus et à renforcer notre efficacité globale.
Au quotidien, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de transformation, de gestion de projet et d’autres départements clés. Vous serez le point de contact privilégié du Lean Development Manager/Transformation Manager, et vous piloterez la mise en œuvre du plan de transformation Lean Development et de la feuille de route IMPACT 30 pour la division P&D VLL.
Vous vous occuperez plus particulièrement de l’accompagnement des équipes dans l’utilisation des principes et outils Lean tels que l’AMDEC, la cartographie des flux de valeur (VSM), la résolution de problèmes, le management visuel et l’OBEYA, mais aussi de la promotion et du suivi des actions de transformation.
 - Nous ferons appel à vous pour : 
 - Former et accompagner les équipes, et animer des ateliers sur les outils Lean tels que l’AMDEC, le VSM et la résolution de problèmes. 
 - Promouvoir l’organisation PM2020 et les principes PDCC. 
 - Coacher les équipes sur la mise en place de l’OBEYA et garantir la cohérence de l’arborescence OBEYA. 
 - Réduire les besoins en reporting et réunions en renforçant le système de management. 
 - Encourager la résolution d’actions et mesurer le déploiement des actions de transformation (méthode DI et transformation OBEYA). 
 - Identifier et consigner de nouvelles actions de transformation lors de votre participation à des OBEYA ou des ateliers. 
 - Analyser et partager les bonnes pratiques de mise en œuvre des actions Lean dans d’autres sites du groupe. 
 - Influencer les décisions au niveau régional et du groupe pour promouvoir les actions clés de performance. 
 - Faire remonter les points bloquants et les alertes (ANDONS) liés à la transformation.

 Nous accordons plus d'importance à la passion et à l’état d’esprit qu'à l'expérience. C'est pourquoi nous n'attendons pas de vous que vous possédiez toutes les compétences. Nous avons plutôt dressé une liste de celles qui, selon nous, vous aideront à réussir et à vous épanouir dans ce rôle :
 - Diplôme en gestion, ingénierie ou dans un domaine pertinent. 
 - Expérience ou compréhension approfondie des principes et outils Lean (AMDEC, VSM, résolution de problèmes, OBEYA, management visuel). 
 - Connaissance des systèmes de gestion de projet et des méthodologies de transformation organisationnelle. 
 - Familiarité avec les environnements industriels, idéalement dans le secteur ferroviaire ou un secteur connexe. 
 - Excellentes compétences en communication et en animation d’ateliers. 
 - Capacité à influencer et à mobiliser des équipes transversales. 
 - Approche orientée résultats avec une forte capacité d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes. 
 Ce que vous apprécierez Rejoignez-nous pour une nouvelle expérience de vie - le secteur ferroviaire est un secteur d’avenir, vous pouvez donc vous développer et acquérir de nouvelles compétences et expériences tout au long de votre carrière. Vous pourrez également :
 - Bénéficier de stabilité, de défis et d'une carrière à long terme sans routine quotidienne. 
 - Travailler avec des équipes passionnées et pluridisciplinaires, dans un environnement où l’innovation et la collaboration sont valorisées. 
 - Collaborer avec des équipes transversales et des collègues qualifiés. 
 - Contribuer à des projets innovants qui façonnent l’avenir de la mobilité. 
 - Utiliser notre environnement de travail flexible et axé sur la performance. 
 - Orienter votre carrière dans la direction de votre choix à travers les fonctions et les pays. 
 - Bénéficier de notre investissement dans votre développement, par le biais de programmes d’apprentissage primés. 
 - Progresser vers des postes de leadership ou des rôles stratégiques au sein de l’entreprise. 
 - Bénéficier d'un système de rémunération équitable et dynamique qui reconnaît vos performances et votre potentiel, ainsi que d'une couverture sociale complète et compétitive (assurance-vie, assurance-maladie, pension). 
 Il n'est pas nécessaire d'être un passionné de trains pour s'épanouir chez nous. Nous vous garantissons que lorsque vous monterez dans l'un de nos trains avec vos amis ou votre famille, vous en serez fier. Si vous êtes prêt à relever le défi, nous aimerions vous connaître !
 Important
 En tant qu'entreprise mondiale, nous sommes un employeur qui prône l'égalité des chances et qui célèbre la diversité dans les 63 pays où nous sommes présents. Nous nous engageons à créer un lieu de travail inclusif pour tous.

 Missions & Responsabilités

 - Contribuer à la définition, la formalisation et la mise à jour des processus ITSM (gestion des incidents, problèmes, changements, etc.)
 - Rédiger et maintenir les procédures, modes opératoires et référentiels de bonnes pratiques
 - Assurer la standardisation et la cohérence des pratiques au sein de la DSI et avec les partenaires
 - Participer à la gestion du catalogue de services et à la définition des SLA/OLA
 - Mettre en place et suivre les tableaux de bord de performance (SLA, MTTR, incidents, qualité de service)
 - Analyser les indicateurs et identifier les axes d’amélioration
 - Piloter les plans d’actions correctives et suivre leur mise en œuvre
 - Identifier les dysfonctionnements récurrents et proposer des actions d’amélioration continue
 - Participer à la capitalisation des retours d’expérience et à l’alimentation de la base de connaissances (REX, incidents, bonnes pratiques)
 - Animer les rituels qualité (revues de service, comités RUN, post-mortem incidents)
 - Assurer la coordination transverse entre les équipes techniques et métiers
 - Contribuer à l’identification et à la gestion des risques liés aux processus SI
 - Veiller au respect des procédures, normes et standards qualité
 - Assurer un reporting régulier auprès de la hiérarchie et des instances de gouvernance
 Livrables attendus
 - Cartographie et documentation des processus SI
 - Procédures et référentiels qualité à jour
 - Tableaux de bord et indicateurs de performance

 At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed.  Travel: ~75% across assigned European manufacturing sites
 Job Purpose
 As an Operations Excellence Engineer, you will play a central role in deploying and embedding a new group manufacturing system across Amcor’s Rigid Packaging division, supporting a large-scale Lean transformation at group level .
The position sits within the Rigid Division of Amcor and reports to the Rigid Quality & CI Director. You will work in close partnership with plant leadership teams, department managers, and shopfloor teams across multiple European countries, acting as a hands-on coach and structured change agent .
This role offers a rare opportunity to drive a large-scale Lean transformation across a complex, multisite European manufacturing network , working at the intersection of strategy and shopfloor execution. You will influence how 10–15 plants operate every day, collaborate with diverse leadership teams across countries and cultures, and play a decisive role in rolling out a common manufacturing system that will shape operational standards across the Rigid Packaging division.
 Principal Responsibilities
 Deploy the new group manufacturing system (Level 2) across 10 to 15 sites:
 - Lead preparation, deployment, and stabilization activities across the plants 
 - Ensure consistency and sustainability of the new manufacturing system practices across plants. 
 Train and coach teams at all levels of the organization: 
 - Teach Lean and manufacturing system tools to plant leadership, department managers, and shopfloor teams, 
 - Act as a hands-on coach to reinforce structured problem-solving, standard work, and daily management routines. 
 Drive change and adoption of continuous improvement ways of working:
 - Support sites with low CI maturity and guide teams through behavioral and operational change, 
 - Address resistance to change through structured engagement and pragmatic change management. 
 Enable alignment and knowledge sharing across the plant network:
 - Capture and share best practices, lessons learned, and standards across sites, 
 - Provide clear progress updates to Quality, CI, and Operations stakeholders. 
 Requirements And Qualifications
 - Engineering degree or equivalent operational experience, 
 - Strong hands-on experience in Lean and Continuous Improvement:
 - Advanced knowledge of Lean tools and methodologies - Lean Six Sigma Black Belt experience strongly preferred,
 - Solid change management capability, including experience deploying CI tools in low-maturity environments,
 - Strong experience in a manufacturing site production environment, with a deep understanding of shopfloor operations, 
 - Fluency in English mandatory, 
 - Professional to fluent French or German strongly recommended, 
 - Proven ability to teach, coach, and influence teams from plant management to shopfloor level. 
 About Amcor
 Amcor is the global leader in developing and producing responsible consumer packaging and dispensing solutions across a variety of materials for nutrition, health, beauty and wellness categories. Our global product innovation and sustainability expertise enables us to solve packaging challenges around the world every day, producing a range of flexible packaging, rigid packaging, cartons and closures that are more sustainable, functional and appealing for our customers and their consumers. We are guided by our purpose of elevating customers, shaping lives and protecting the future. Supported by a commitment to safety, over 75,000 people generate $23 billion in annualized sales from operations that span over 400 locations in more than 40 countries.

 About the Role 
 We are partnering with a leading global manufacturing company to appoint a Global Continuous Improvement Director to lead enterprise-wide Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement initiatives across its international manufacturing footprint.
 This is a newly created leadership position supporting the company's rapid global expansion. Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the successful candidate will drive Lean transformation, operational excellence, and business performance improvements across multiple manufacturing sites worldwide.
 Key Responsibilities 
 - Develop and execute the global Continuous Improvement strategy aligned with business objectives.
 - Lead Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and business transformation initiatives across multiple international manufacturing sites.
 - Establish standardized Continuous Improvement frameworks, governance, and best practices globally.

 - Lead and develop a global Continuous Improvement team while coaching regional and site-level CI leaders.

 - Proven track record of driving Lean transformation across multiple manufacturing sites or regions.
 - Strong experience working with cross-functional and multicultural teams.
 - Excellent stakeholder management and leadership skills.
 - Fluent English communication skills are essential.
 Preferred Background

 - Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, Six Sigma, and business transformation methodologies.

 What We're Looking For 
 - Strong influencing skills with the ability to engage senior stakeholders globally.

 Brink’s is seeking a dynamic and strategic Director of Lean Operations to lead the enterprise-wide transformation toward operational excellence. This high-impact role will drive continuous improvement initiatives that elevate performance, increase efficiency, and deliver measurable business results across all lines of business. The ideal candidate will be a change agent, coach, and enterprise partner—bringing Lean principles to life in a complex, service-driven environment.
 This role may be based at Brink's Headquarters in Coppell, TX, or within the Midwest/Mid-Atlantic operating region, including Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Kentucky, Maryland, Virginia, Washington, D.C., and surrounding markets. 
 ** Must be willing to travel 50% to 70% for this role. ** 
 Key Responsibilities 
 · Strategic Execution: Lead the development and implementation of Lean strategies that directly support business growth, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction at the national level.
 · Cultural Transformation: Champion a culture of continuous improvement, embedding Lean thinking across all functions and levels of the organization—from frontline teams to senior leadership.
 · Operational Road mapping: Own and execute the Lean Roadmap, ensuring consistent adoption of core methodologies (5S, A3 Problem Solving, VSM, Standard Work, Visual Management, TPM) across regions and business units.
 · Leadership Engagement: Partner with operational leaders to define performance expectations, deliver coaching, and develop leadership capability in Lean thinking and behaviors.
 · Kaizen & Value Stream Optimization: Facilitate regional Kaizen events and improvement workshops, targeting high-impact areas to eliminate waste, streamline workflows, and improve service delivery.
 · Standardization & Scalability: Identify and institutionalize best practices across all locations, ensuring scalable, repeatable processes and sustainable results.

 · Strategic Program Management: Lead critical, enterprise-level projects focused on operational efficiency—including production planning, logistics routing, resource optimization, and workforce deployment.
 What You Bring

 · Operational Grit: Willingness to engage directly with operations teams, lead from the front, and model Lean behaviors.
 · Influence & Collaboration: Strong presence with the ability to align, influence, and inspire cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
 · Exceptional Communication: Clear and direct communicator with the ability to engage all levels of the organization.
 · Analytical Mindset: Data-driven and process-centric with a relentless focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence.
 · Change Agent: Confident navigating ambiguity and driving change in a matrixed, fast-paced environment.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 · Brink’s Bronze or Silver Lean Leader certification strongly preferred
 · Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, or related field
 · 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence roles
 · Multi-site operations or logistics industry experience is a plus
